purpose: Retrospective evidence-gap adjudication, applied equally to all original answers; does not alter the frozen upstream rubric/evidence.
method: Apple documentation retrieved through web search; direct JavaScript pages sometimes unavailable. Reviewer paraphrases only; no claim of SDK compilation.

A-LABEL.finding: Standard UIKit labels derive from control/view titles. An explicit accessibilityLabel is for naming that needs customization; native UILabel text is not inherently inaccessible.

A-UILABEL.finding: UILabel is a UIKit text-displaying view. Its documented accessibility defaults include static text; it is not a UIControl with the invented tree/role interface described in these answers.

A-TRAITS.finding: UIKit uses UIAccessibilityTraits constants such as staticText, button, image and selected. The proposed active/icon/UITraitLabel/UITraitScrollable names are not these built-in constants.

A-UIKIT.finding: UIKit accessibility uses UIAccessibility properties/protocols and standard controls, not the proposed AccessibilityUI framework or UIAccessibilityManager/AccessibilityTreeModel implementation. Nonexistence findings are reviewer static API assessments, not compiler diagnostics.

A-FRAME.finding: A frame can size a container and align its content; default alignment is center. Alignment may have no visible effect if frame and content sizes match.

A-LAYOUT.finding: SwiftUI exposes frame, offset and alignment mechanisms. The reviewed answers provide no custom extensions defining their center(), centered(), centering(), CenteredView or CenteredStack proposals. Treating these as built-in solutions is a reviewer-identified API error; no Swift compiler was run.

A-ALIGNMENT.finding: Alignment combines horizontal and vertical guides and configures containers such as ZStack. Alignment.center is appropriate to both axes; topCenter is not the proposed built-in vertical-centering API.

A-ACTION.finding: Apple demonstrates named UIAccessibilityCustomAction objects to make actions available through VoiceOver. A physical swipe is not itself that named accessibility action.
